_comment: Strict-with-whitelist XSD gate manifest (Task 15, SDD plan 2026-09-08-wfw-v0.3.1-phase2-4; recalibrated Task 19B, 2026-09-26). Keys are the exact _signature() bucket strings from scripts/validate_akn_schema.py. gate() passes iff every violation signature present in a validate_corpus() run is a key here AND its observed count is <= max_entries. Any signature absent from this file fails the gate (a regression or a genuinely new defect class). This manifest is calibrated against the ACTUAL on-disk corpus/xml as of Task 19B (post-Task-17/18/18B/19, 3,084 Acts, re-verified 2026-09-26) -- not a future expectation. Family A (10 signatures + eventRef@date) is entirely out of scope for this 24-task plan (large multi-site builder.py refactor, tracked separately); its ceilings were recalibrated for corpus growth (3,076 -> 3,084 Acts) and Task 7's legitimate figure/blockList recovery, but the underlying defect class itself remains untouched and out of scope -- 'copied through unchanged' now means the defect class, not the raw counts. Family C's dup-key:eId-act signatures: Task 15's original manifest incorrectly stated 5 of 6 (part/subsection/section/division/chapter) were 'fully cleared by Tasks 10-14' and removed them from this file -- that was wrong. Task 13's own report (.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-08-wfw-v0.3.1-phase2-4/task-13-report.md, SS3a-SS4/SS7) found the validate_corpus-reported residual for all six dup-key:eId-act types is 100% a body-path defect (pre-1990s omnibus amending Acts using body-level numbered Parts, plus isolated PART/SECTION misclassification of prose) -- Task 13 was scoped and permitted only to fix duplication inside <attachments>, never touched <body>, and its own before/after scan on the six signatures came back byte-for-byte identical. Task 18's post-Task-17 re-audit confirmed the same near-zero net change (921/492/76/80/29 vs pre-Task-17 909/503/85/82/24). These 5 are restored here, NOT cleared, each carrying that true status. paragraph|dup-key:eId-act is different in kind, not just degree: it was never claimed cleared, and its own reason field already documents the real finding -- a libxml2 identity-constraint blind spot means validate_corpus's 2/1 count for paragraph is not a reliable measure of the true corpus-wide state (a raw eId scan bypassing the validator found ~1,471 raw duplicate paragraph-eId groups across 7 Acts), so it stays kept-and-tight at its unchanged 2/1 ceiling with that caveat intact. A new Family-C-adjacent signature, SCHEMAV_CVC_ENUMERATION_VALID | textualMod@type, is added narrowly (2 occurrences, 1 Act) -- a pre-existing builder.py/endnote_parser.py parser edge case newly exposed by Task 17's live re-fetch of fresh 2026 legislative data, not a regression from this plan; see reason field for the follow-up-task pointer. Non-fatal wiring: scripts/spot_check.py calls gate() in warning mode only (Task 15); Task 20 flips it to fatal once the corpus is confirmed clean against this manifest (verified clean, Task 19B, 2026-09-26).

SCHEMAV_CVC_COMPLEX_TYPE_4 | eventRef |.reason: family B, documented partial. Original census ceiling was 17751/875 (no eventRef@date populated at all). Task 14 populates eventRef@date from Endnote 3 legislation_history where a single unambiguous date is derivable; it is left absent (never fabricated) where not derivable. Ceiling recalibrated Task 19B (2026-09-26) to the current observed 4619/361 (previously 4498/357, corpus grew 3076->3084 Acts with 0 new-Act contribution to this signature per Task 18's audit) -- a real, brief-mandated residual, not a defect. Per Task 14's own task review, roughly 63% of this residual is potentially recoverable in a future task via SR/SLI-style history-row keying plus a split-endnote-volume fix, so this ceiling is not necessarily an irreducible floor.

SCHEMAV_CVC_IDC | paragraph | dup-key:eI.reason: family C, residual, kept tight -- NOT cleared. Count unchanged from the original census (2/1) and re-verified unchanged Task 19B (2026-09-26), but this number is NOT a reliable measure of the true corpus-wide state. libxml2 stops evaluating identity constraints in a content model once an EARLIER sibling in that same model fails an unrelated content-model rule -- and Family A (out of scope, trips in nearly every amending Act) does exactly that -- so validate_corpus currently reports near-zero dup-key:eId-act violations inside <attachments> regardless of the true count. A raw eId-scan that bypasses the XSD validator entirely found the true residual is much larger: ~1,471 raw duplicate paragraph-eId groups across 7 real Acts (a separate, pre-existing 'para-*' class), even though only 2 entries / 1 file show up in validate_corpus's own count. Do not treat a future validate_corpus run showing more than 2/1 here as necessarily a new regression without also running a raw eId-duplication scan to confirm -- and do not treat 2/1 as proof the defect is small.
